summary:
EARTHWISE is a crop-rotation decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It uses NASA POWER Earth observation data, including historical rainfall, temperature, humidity, and root-zone soil wetness, alongside farmer-provided soil information and crop characteristics to help explore suitable crop-rotation strategies.

EARTHWISE offers two user experiences through one connected platform. Farmer Mode provides a simple, multilingual (English, Sinhala, and Tamil) step-by-step interface that makes agricultural insights accessible to farmers with limited technical experience. Expert Mode provides researchers and agricultural specialists with detailed climate visualizations, soil data inputs, adjustable decision priorities, and transparent comparisons of crop-rotation scenarios.

Initially focused on Sri Lanka's Dry Zone, EARTHWISE addresses the challenge of making NASA Earth observation data useful for practical agricultural decisions. By connecting satellite-derived environmental information with local farming needs, it aims to support more informed crop planning, soil-health considerations, and climate-resilient agriculture.
details:
EarthWise is a platform designed to help farmers make better crop rotation decisions using NASA satellite and climate data. It combines historical climate observations, soil information, and crop characteristics to explore suitable crop rotation strategies.

The platform has two modes. Farmer Mode provides a simple step-by-step experience where farmers can select their language, choose their farm location, select crops, and view suggested crop rotation strategies. It supports English, Sinhala, and Tamil, making agricultural information more accessible to farmers with limited technical knowledge. Expert Mode provides researchers and agricultural specialists with detailed climate visualisations, historical rainfall and temperature information, soil data inputs, interactive maps, adjustable priorities, and crop rotation comparisons.

We use NASA POWER as our main source of historical climate information, alongside farmer-provided soil details and agricultural research. The system evaluates different crop sequences and compares three rotation strategies to help users understand their relative suitability. A contextual help assistant is also included to guide users through the platform.

We developed EarthWise using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. We used Leaflet for interactive maps, Recharts for data visualisations, Google Gemini API for the help assistant, and Vitest for testing. NASA POWER is integrated through our backend API routes, with optional Meteomatics integration for supplementary weather forecasts.

Our initial focus is Sri Lanka's Dry Zone, using Padaviya in Anuradhapura as the starting pilot location. We considered the different needs of farmers and researchers, local crop calendars, soil conditions, water requirements, seasonal rainfall patterns, and the limitations of satellite data. Our aim is to make scientific information easier to understand while supporting more informed agricultural planning.

Data Sources and Agricultural References

EarthWise uses NASA POWER for historical climate observations and refers to Sri Lankan agricultural research and official publications to support its crop information and decision-making logic. These include:

  • Department of Agriculture – Rice Research and Development Institute, Mahailluppallama: Rice water-management information and seasonal water requirements. View reference.
  • Gunawardhana et al. (2014), Annals of the Sri Lanka Department of Agriculture: Research on mung bean crop coefficients and water requirements in the DL1b agro-ecological region. Read research paper.
  • Liyanage and related research on residual soil moisture: Research on interseasonal cropping and the use of residual moisture in Sri Lankan paddy fields. View AGRIS reference.
  • Department of Agriculture – RARDC Kilinochchi: Cowpea cultivation information, including growing conditions, waterlogging sensitivity, and crop duration. View crop information.
  • Karunarathna (2006), Annals of the Sri Lanka Department of Agriculture: Research on maize inbred lines and hybrids developed at Maha Illuppallama. Read research paper.
  • Ministry of Agriculture, Sri Lanka (2025): Official agricultural statistics and cultivation targets for Maha 2024/25 and Yala 2025, including other field crops. View publication.
  • Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO): Agricultural and seasonal reference information for understanding Sri Lanka's Maha and Yala cultivation cycles. View FAO report.
  • Department of Agriculture – National Agriculture Information and Communication Centre: Official crop calendars for paddy, green gram, cowpea, maize, black gram, and other crops. View crop calendars.

These references provide the agricultural foundation for the platform. We also recognise that crop requirements can vary according to location, soil, irrigation, and seasonal conditions, so reference values and model assumptions need appropriate local validation.
